books.title: Ganita Prakash: Textbook of Mathematics for Grade 7, Part I
Ganita Prakash: Textbook of Mathematics for Grade 7, Part II
books.edition: First Edition October 2025; the prelims and chapter PDFs carry no 'Reprint 2026-27' mark

source.method: chapter titles from the book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's section headings

topics.title: A Lakh Varieties!
objectives: Student can get a sense of large quantities by comparing them with familiar ones, such as a height compared with a known building
Student can reason about whether one lakh is a large or a small number in different contexts
visualIdeas: a line of 1 lakh people stretching 38 km
a tall statue compared with a stack of familiar objects

topics.title: Reading and Writing Numbers
objectives: Student can place commas in large numbers using the Indian place value system
Student can read and write the number names of numbers in lakhs
visualIdeas: a place value chart up to ten lakhs with comma positions

topics.title: Land of Tens
objectives: Student can find how many presses of a +1000, +10,000 or +1,00,000 button are needed to reach a given number
Student can use place value to build numbers from tens, hundreds, thousands and lakhs in the fewest steps
visualIdeas: calculators with only +10, +100, +1000 buttons

topics.title: Of Crores and Crores!
objectives: Student can read and write numbers in both the Indian system (lakh, crore, arab) and the American/International system (million, billion)
Student can convert between the systems, for example 10 lakh = 1 million and 100 crore = 1 billion
visualIdeas: two rows of the same number with Indian and International comma placement

topics.title: Exact and Approximate Values
objectives: Student can decide when an exact number is needed and when an approximation is enough
Student can find the nearest thousand, ten thousand, lakh, ten lakh and crore of a large number
Student can compare and round city populations from a census table
visualIdeas: a number line showing a number between its nearest lakhs
a table of city populations

topics.title: Patterns in Products
objectives: Student can use shortcuts such as multiplying by 5 as dividing by 2 and multiplying by 10
Student can predict the number of digits in a product from the numbers being multiplied
visualIdeas: 116 x 5 = 58 x 10 written as a step diagram
multiplication patterns like 11 x 11, 111 x 111

topics.title: Did You Ever Wonder...?
objectives: Student can answer thought-experiment questions with large numbers, such as whether the population of Mumbai could fit into 1 lakh buses
Student can make reasonable assumptions and estimates to work through such questions
visualIdeas: a long line of buses next to a crowd representing Mumbai

topics.title: Simple Expressions
objectives: Student can write an arithmetic expression for a situation and find its value
Student can compare expressions using =, < and > by reasoning, without always evaluating them
visualIdeas: an expression card 5 x 25 linked to a weekly lunch cost
two expressions on a balance scale

topics.title: Brackets in Expressions
objectives: Student can explain how brackets show the order of operations in an expression
Student can evaluate expressions containing brackets
visualIdeas: 30 + (5 x 4) with the bracket highlighted and evaluated first

topics.title: Terms in Expressions
objectives: Student can identify the terms of an expression as the parts separated by + signs
Student can evaluate an expression without brackets by first evaluating its terms
visualIdeas: an expression split into coloured term boxes

topics.title: Swapping and Grouping
objectives: Student can explain that swapping (commutative property) and grouping (associative property) the terms of a sum does not change its value
Student can use swapping and grouping to evaluate expressions quickly, including terms with a minus sign
visualIdeas: terms written on cards being swapped and grouped

topics.title: More Expressions and Their Terms
objectives: Student can write expressions with several terms for real-life situations such as a bill with a tip
Student can identify the terms of such expressions correctly
visualIdeas: a restaurant bill shown as 4 x 23 + 5

topics.title: Removing Brackets I
objectives: Student can explain that removing a bracket preceded by a minus sign changes the sign of each term inside it
Student can simplify expressions like 200 - (40 + 3) in two ways

topics.title: Tinker the Terms I
objectives: Student can predict how the value of an expression changes when one of its terms increases or decreases
Student can find the new value with as little computation as possible, for example when a term -16 becomes -15 the value increases by 1
visualIdeas: a table of expressions with one term changed and the new value

topics.title: Removing Brackets II
objectives: Student can apply the distributive property: multiplying a number by a bracketed sum equals multiplying it by each term
Student can use the distributive property to evaluate products like 2 x (43 + 24)
visualIdeas: an area model showing 2 x (43 + 24) = 2 x 43 + 2 x 24

topics.title: Tinker the Terms II
objectives: Student can use a known product to find a related product, for example 63 x 18 from 53 x 18
Student can find quick ways to evaluate products like 97 x 25
visualIdeas: 63 x 18 drawn as (53 + 10) x 18

topics.title: The Need for Smaller Units
objectives: Student can explain why a unit is split into smaller parts to measure more accurately
Student can describe a length that lies between two whole units, such as the size of a screw
visualIdeas: a screw measured against a ruler with and without smaller markings

topics.title: A Tenth Part
objectives: Student can express a length as units and tenths, for example 3 units and 4 tenths
Student can state that 10 one-tenths make one unit
visualIdeas: a ruler with one unit split into 10 equal parts

topics.title: A Hundredth Part
objectives: Student can explain that each tenth can be split into 10 hundredths and that 100 hundredths make one unit
Student can express measurements in units, tenths and hundredths
visualIdeas: a magnified tenth on a ruler split into 10 hundredths

topics.title: Decimal Place Value
objectives: Student can extend the place value table to tenths, hundredths and thousandths
Student can write, read and expand decimal numbers using the decimal point
visualIdeas: a place value chart with columns from hundreds to thousandths

topics.title: Units of Measurement
objectives: Student can convert lengths between mm, cm, m and km using decimals
Student can convert weights between g and kg and money between paise and rupees using decimals
visualIdeas: a ruler showing 12 mm = 1.2 cm
a 254 g packet labelled 0.254 kg

topics.title: Locating and Comparing Decimals
objectives: Student can locate decimals on the number line and compare them
Student can explain why 0.2, 0.20 and 0.200 are equal
Student can find which decimal is closest to a given number
visualIdeas: a number line between 1 and 2 divided into tenths with 1.4 marked

topics.title: Addition and Subtraction of Decimals
objectives: Student can add and subtract decimals using place value
Student can continue decimal sequences and estimate sums and differences of decimals
visualIdeas: 2.7 m + 3.5 m of cloth shown as place value columns

topics.title: More on the Decimal System
objectives: Student can explain how decimal point and unit-conversion mistakes have caused real problems
Student can explain why 4.5 hours is 4 hours 30 minutes and not 4:50
Student can describe how decimal notation developed over time in India
visualIdeas: a clock showing 4.5 hours after noon as 4:30

topics.title: The Notion of Letter-Numbers
objectives: Student can use a letter-number to stand for an unknown or varying quantity, such as an age
Student can write and evaluate simple formulas with letter-numbers
visualIdeas: two age counters: Aftab a and Shabnam a + 3

topics.title: Revisiting Arithmetic Expressions
objectives: Student can apply swapping and grouping of terms and brackets to expressions with letter-numbers
Student can write an expression as a sum of terms and read it without confusion
visualIdeas: an expression written as a sum of terms with a letter-number term

topics.title: Omission of the Multiplication Symbol in Algebraic Expressions
objectives: Student can write products such as 4 x n as 4n
Student can describe a sequence such as the multiples of 4 with an algebraic expression
Student can find and correct mistakes when letter-numbers are replaced by numbers
visualIdeas: the sequence 4, 8, 12, ... with the nth term 4n

topics.title: Simplification of Algebraic Expressions
objectives: Student can find the perimeter of a rectangle as an algebraic expression
Student can simplify algebraic expressions by combining like terms
Student can identify and correct mistakes in simplifications
visualIdeas: a rectangle labelled l and b with perimeter 2l + 2b

topics.title: Formula Detective
objectives: Student can find the formula used by a number machine from examples of its inputs and outputs
Student can write the number machine's formula as an algebraic expression and test it on new inputs
visualIdeas: a Y-shaped number machine taking two inputs and giving one output

topics.title: Algebraic Expressions to Describe Patterns
objectives: Student can describe the positions of a repeating design with an expression like 3n
Student can use algebra to explain patterns in a calendar, such as equal diagonal sums in a 2 x 2 square
visualIdeas: a saree border with repeating designs A, B, C
a calendar with a 2 x 2 square marked

topics.title: Matchstick Patterns
objectives: Student can find the number of matchsticks needed at any step of a pattern using an algebraic expression
Student can draw the next step of a matchstick pattern and explain how the expression counts its sticks
visualIdeas: matchstick triangles growing step by step

topics.title: Across the Line
objectives: Student can identify that two intersecting lines form four angles, with vertically opposite angles equal and linear pairs adding to 180°
Student can explain how measurement errors can make measured angles differ from these facts
visualIdeas: two crossing lines with the four angles coloured

topics.title: Perpendicular Lines
objectives: Student can explain that if two lines intersect and all four angles are equal, each angle is 90° and the lines are perpendicular
Student can identify perpendicular lines in the surroundings and in figures
visualIdeas: two perpendicular lines with right-angle marks

topics.title: Between Lines
objectives: Student can describe how line segments meet or cross using terms like point, endpoint, midpoint and intersect, with angle measures
Student can recognise parallel lines as lines on a plane that never meet
visualIdeas: segments meeting at endpoints and crossing at midpoints

topics.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines in Paper Folding
objectives: Student can make parallel and perpendicular creases by folding paper
Student can use arrow marks for parallel lines and a square mark for perpendicular lines
visualIdeas: a folded sheet with parallel and perpendicular creases marked

topics.title: Transversals
objectives: Student can identify a transversal as a line that intersects a pair of lines and the 8 angles it forms
Student can draw a transversal to a pair of lines and label the angles it forms
visualIdeas: a transversal crossing two lines with 8 numbered angles

topics.title: Corresponding Angles
objectives: Student can identify pairs of corresponding angles
Student can state that corresponding angles are equal when a transversal cuts parallel lines, and that lines are parallel if corresponding angles are equal
visualIdeas: corresponding angles highlighted in matching colours

topics.title: Drawing Parallel Lines
objectives: Student can draw parallel lines with a ruler and a set square
Student can make a line parallel to a given line through a given point by paper folding
visualIdeas: a set square sliding along a ruler

topics.title: Alternate Angles
objectives: Student can identify alternate angles and show they are equal when a transversal cuts parallel lines
Student can show that interior angles on the same side of a transversal add up to 180°
visualIdeas: a Z-shape highlighting alternate angles

topics.title: Parallel Illusions
objectives: Student can recognise parallel lines in optical illusions where they appear not to be parallel
Student can check with a ruler or by measuring whether lines in an illusion are really parallel
visualIdeas: a figure of straight parallel lines that appear slanted because of the pattern around them

topics.title: Numbers Tell us Things
objectives: Student can work out the numbers children call out when each says how many taller children stand in front of them
Student can arrange heights to produce a given sequence of called-out numbers, or explain why it is impossible
visualIdeas: stick figures of different heights in a row with numbers above them

topics.title: Picking Parity
objectives: Student can determine whether a sum or product is even or odd without calculating it
Student can find the parity of the number of small squares in a grid from its dimensions
Student can find expressions like 2n that always have even parity
visualIdeas: number cards that cannot sum to 30
a 3 x 4 grid with paired squares

topics.title: Some Explorations in Grids
objectives: Student can fill a 3 x 3 grid with the numbers 1-9 to meet given row and column sums or explain why it is impossible
Student can construct 3 x 3 magic squares
visualIdeas: a 3 x 3 grid with circled row and column sums

topics.title: Generalising a 3 x 3 Magic Square
objectives: Student can describe the structure of a 3 x 3 magic square in terms of the centre number m
Student can explore the Chautisa Yantra, the first recorded 4 x 4 magic square, and magic squares in history and culture
visualIdeas: a magic square with entries written as m + 1, m - 3, ...
the Chautisa Yantra grid

topics.title: Nature's Favourite Sequence: The Virahanka-Fibonacci Numbers!
objectives: Student can continue the Virahanka sequence 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ... by adding the two previous numbers
Student can explain how these numbers arose from counting rhythms of long and short syllables in Indian poetry
visualIdeas: rhythms of short and long syllables counted for 1 to 5 beats

topics.title: Digits in Disguise
objectives: Student can solve cryptarithms where letters stand for digits
Student can use reasoning about carries and place value to find which digit each letter stands for
visualIdeas: T + T = UT written with letter tiles

topics.title: Two Angles and the Included Side
